name: Pellucid BioClean Class-1 Geneware Lab Suit
description:
A cleanroom suit designed for Class-1 geneware fabrication environments and high-grade biotech labs. The outer shell is ultrasonic-welded polyethylene fabric in sterile white with fine silver anti-static threading — new suits are blinding white; worn ones carry a faint yellowish cast from sterilization fluid cycling. Hood is integrated with a sealed polycarbonate visor and positive-pressure filtered air delivery at the collar.

Every seam is smooth-faced inward to prevent particulate shedding. Gloves are separate but connect via sterile-lock ring cuffs. The suit design accommodates tail and horn geneware through sealed elasticated apertures at the base of the spine and crown — apertures ship sealed and are field-opened by the user. Used in Tier 4-5 labs but also smuggled into unlicensed Shelf geneware clinics.
functionality: Class-1 cleanroom rated — less than 10 particles per cubic foot. Positive-pressure air delivery prevents contaminant ingress. Anti-static threading prevents charge buildup near sensitive biotech equipment. Sealed gene-compatible apertures at spine base and crown. Neural port access panel at rear collar for BCI techs working in sterile environments.
what_it_says: You work with things precise enough that your body is the contamination risk.
manufacturer: Pellucid BioSystems (Tier 4-5 licensed); stolen/surplus units reach Shelf clinics
story_hooks: A Shelf geneware clinic is performing unlicensed modifications using stolen Pellucid suits — the suits are legitimate, but nothing else in the operating space is.
A lab technician notices their suit's positive-pressure system has been quietly downgraded — someone wanted a specific sample to get out of the cleanroom.
The sealed gene-apertures on a batch of suits were shipped pre-opened, suggesting someone at the factory is flagging suits for buyers who don't want to ask questions about their modifications.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A full-body cleanroom coverall that reads as clinical and otherworldly—pristine white with a sealed hood and integrated visor that obscures the wearer's face entirely. The silhouette is loose but structured, with deliberate apertures at the spine and crown that hint at augmentation compatibility. Moves with a whisper-quiet, synthetic quality.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through torso and limbs to accommodate layering and movement in lab environments; sealed at wrists, ankles, and neck via friction-fit elasticated cuffs. Hood pulls tight around the face. Designed for function over form.
physical_description.primary_material: Ultrasonic-welded polyethylene fabric with silver anti-static threading woven throughout. Polycarbonate visor panel. Elasticated seals at apertures.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost frictionless outer surface with sealed inward seams. The visor is optically clear but slightly frosted from microbial coating. Silver threading creates a subtle grid pattern visible under close inspection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Sterile white with fine silver anti-static grid. Yellowing along seams and visor edges indicates age and sterilization fluid exposure. Faint brownish discoloration at geneware apertures from repeated field-opening.
physical_description.closures: Positive-pressure sealed collar with filtered air delivery nozzle. Wrist and ankle cuffs with sterile-lock ring connectors for gloves. Sealed geneware apertures ship closed; user opens via controlled tear or heat-activation.
distinctive_features: Integrated polycarbonate visor with anti-fog micro-etching
Sealed elasticated apertures at base of spine and crown for tail/horn geneware
Smooth-faced inward seams to prevent particulate shedding
Positive-pressure filtered air delivery system at collar
Sterile-lock ring cuff connectors (gloves sold separately)
Faint sterilization fluid yellowing on worn units
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5: Licensed biotech equipment designed for high-grade geneware labs. Stolen surplus reaches unlicensed Shelf clinics and black-market modification clinics.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by legitimate biotech technicians and unauthorized geneware modders. Signals either professional credentials or dangerous underground work. In the Shelf, it reads as 'someone who modifies augmentations'—either clinician or desperate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine factory units are blinding white with perfect seals. Used units show yellowing, faint discoloration at apertures from repeated opening, micro-scratches on visor, and a faint chemical smell from sterilization cycling. Some show burn marks where sealed apertures were force-opened with heated tools.
